Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 2.3 item 2 (Black Cleaver average stacks)
sources_quoted.quote: the established model uses a fixed `0.8*max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +-20% at the extremes. The stack duration (6 s) is always longer than the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic AS*u > 1/6, so expiry does not rescue the constant - this is a documented tuning constant, not a theorem. Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean when a champion module needs exact BC numbers

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 5 formula-audit table, row 'Terminus/BC ramps'
sources_quoted.quote: Terminus/BC ramps (`average_pen`, `average_reduction`) | Cesaro mean of the per-hit ramp | APPROX | m(R) convex => averaging understates ramp damage (Jensen); BC constant = exact mean at ~10 autos, +-20% at extremes
m(R) = 100 / (100 + R) ... R_final = max(0, (R - r_flat)*(1 - r_pct/100)*(1 - p) - f) ... flat reduction -> percentage reduction -> percentage penetration -> flat penetration

step_1_reconstruct_the_ramp_from_cached_.statement: Carve caps at C = 5 stacks at 6% armor reduction each (30% max). Hit i of a stream sees min(i, C) stacks (the hit applies its own stack before its damage is mitigated, per the engine ordering convention quoted in Section 2.3).
step_1_reconstruct_the_ramp_from_cached_.conclusion: I re-derived the closed form independently and it reproduces docs/math-foundations.md exactly.

step_2_cross_check_the_docs_own_calibrat.claim_in_doc: the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos
step_2_cross_check_the_docs_own_calibrat.result: Confirmed. The doc's '~10 autos' is exact for the wiki's C = 5, which independently corroborates that the engine's max_stacks is 5 (not 6) and per-stack reduction is 6%.

step_3_old_vs_new_model_values.old_constant_model: 0.8 * C = 4.000 stacks -> 24.0% armor reduction (with a hits/2 branch for h < 8)
step_3_old_vs_new_model_values.sign_test: 5 - 10/h > 4  <=>  h > 10. For any sustained roster fight with more than 10 Carve-applying physical hits the exact mean exceeds the constant, so post-fix armor is LOWER and outgoing damage must go UP. Observed change is +84.0 (3226.1 -> 3310.1, +2.6038%): correct sign.

step_4_magnitude_feasibility_band.model: Under the quoted ordering (reduction before penetration) and m(R) = 100/(100+R), the damage ratio for the physical portion is (100 + A*(1 - 0.24)) / (100 + A*(1 - r_new)) with r_new = 0.30 - 0.60/h and A the target's pre-Carve effective armor.
step_4_magnitude_feasibility_band.ceiling_of_the_correct_model: h -> infinity gives r_new = 30% (the wiki cap). Then the ratio is (100+0.76A)/(100+0.70A), which reaches 1.0260376 at A = 62.3 and grows with A (e.g. +3.53% at A = 100).
step_4_magnitude_feasibility_band.verdict_on_magnitude: +2.6038% is comfortably INSIDE the band achievable by the correct C = 5 / 30%-cap model for ordinary level-18 armor values (73-237 effective armor at 25-100 Carve-applying hits, more if part of the damage is magic/true and therefore unaffected). The change does not require exceeding the wiki's 30% cap, so it is not evidence of an over-capped (e.g. C = 6 / 36%) implementation.
step_4_magnitude_feasibility_band.note: The band is one-sided: it rules out an implausibly large jump, it cannot by itself pin the exact 3310.1.

step_5_what_i_could_not_do.limitation: The scenario tuple for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (champions, levels, ranks, item sets, target stats, fight window, roster composition) is NOT present anywhere in the permitted evidence tree — it lives in scripts/, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids reading. Exhaustive grep over the whole export for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster', 'coupled_scenario', 'outgoing_damage_before_death' and 'roster' returned no scenario definition.
step_5_what_i_could_not_do.consequence: This receipt verifies the CHANGE at the mechanism/closed-form/bound level rather than by reproducing 3310.1 arithmetically end to end. The absolute number is not independently re-derivable from data/ + docs/math-foundations.md alone.

alternative_hypothesis_considered.hypothesis: The delta comes from Bloodsong's Expose Weakness melee/ranged split ({{rd|8%|5%}}) rather than from Black Cleaver's stack model.
alternative_hypothesis_considered.fit: A global outgoing amp moving 1+0.05u -> 1+0.08u reproduces ratio 1.0260376 at debuff uptime u = 0.907 (equivalently, ~91% of the 3226.1 sitting under Expose Weakness). Arithmetically admissible.
alternative_hypothesis_considered.why_not_selected: (a) docs/math-foundations.md contains an explicit, standing recommendation to make exactly the Black Cleaver change, flags the old constant as 'a documented tuning constant, not a theorem', and warns it 're-tunes every BC fight in the corpus' - which matches a broad golden re-baseline; (b) the Bloodsong reading requires the ranged branch to have been in force for a holder that should have used the melee branch, which the cached wiki text alone cannot adjudicate without the roster composition; (c) the scenario name pairs both items because it is a coupled item-interaction fixture, so the name is not evidence about which item moved.
alternative_hypothesis_considered.impact_on_verdict: Both readings put the CORRECTED value above the old one (the exact Cesaro mean exceeds the constant for h > 10; the melee branch 8% exceeds the ranged branch 5%). Neither admissible reading makes 3226.1 the corrected number, which is why the verdict is not old_value_correct.

reasoning_summary: Cached wiki text pins Black Cleaver's Carve at 5 stacks x 6% = 30% max armor reduction. I independently derived the exact Cesaro mean of the capped stack ramp, C - C(C-1)/(2h), reproducing the closed form quoted in docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3, and confirmed its calibration claim (the old 0.8*max_stacks = 4-stack constant equals the exact mean at exactly h = 10 when C = 5). The exact mean strictly exceeds the constant for h > 10, so a sustained roster fight must deal MORE damage under the exact model - matching the observed +84.0 (+2.6038%). The magnitude sits inside the feasible band of the correct 30%-capped model for ordinary level-18 effective armor, requiring no cap violation. The old value instantiates a tuning constant the repo's own math foundations document identifies as an approximation with up to +-20% error and explicitly recommends replacing with this closed form; the new value instantiates the exact mean.
caveats: Not an end-to-end arithmetic reproduction of 3310.1: the scenario input tuple is outside the permitted evidence tree.

The Cesaro/average-reduction model is itself a Jensen approximation to a true per-hit ramp (docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3: m(R) is convex in R, so mitigating every hit at the mean reduction UNDERSTATES the true ramp damage). Both 3226.1 and 3310.1 are therefore lower bounds on an exact per-hit simulation; 3310.1 is the strictly better of the two, but a future per-hit implementation should land slightly higher still.
Verdict selects the better-supported of two admissible readings of the delta; both readings agree the corrected value is the higher one.
